title: Block unsupported scores in code
statement: Enforce in code the limits on what a score may claim, so no unvalidated score or prediction of a real test appears until evidence supports it.
example: Two audits found a figure drifting between documents, 0.930 in one and 0.928 in another.
detail: The case for approval of a pre-pilot proxy for an outside reading test enforces its claims ladder in code: before a pilot the engine returns only a logit with its standard error and domain sub-scores, and the RIT, percentile and CGP scales are blocked, so a score report cannot be misread into a claim the number would carry, because the number is not in the response (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5_build_2026_07_02/mapproxy_clean.md`). It gives the reason that two audits had found number drift in its documents, 0.930 against 0.928, so the gate that carries the claim lives in code, not prose. The limits cover any score on an outside test's scale, and the evidence that lifts them can be a linking study of the same students taking both tests close together.
against: Code has faults of its own: one AP benchmark's scorer reads a missing score on a hard-fail dimension as 1.0, a pass (`APinceptbench/benchmark_official.py`).
